description: Labeled cases for cite_audit.py — the in-text/bibliography cross-diff that the citation gate is built on. Positives cover the blocking defects (a key cited but absent from the .bib, a leftover [CITATION NEEDED], a leftover [MATERIAL GAP] in both its English and Turkish spelling) and the non-blocking reports (an orphan bib entry, a cited entry lacking verified={true}, an authorized [LLM-SUPPLEMENTED] fill). The negatives are the shapes that look like citations and are not: a key inside a fenced code block, a key inside inline code, an email address, and STATUS.md — which is a project state file the audit must never scan.

cases.comment: The defect this whole gate exists for: prose cites a source the bibliography does not contain.

cases.comment: Distinct from [CITATION NEEDED]: no session material covers this and the writer refused to fill it from model memory. Same weight, different meaning.

The Turkish spelling [KANIT YOK] must weigh exactly the same as the English one — the kit's central claim is that the two languages are equal targets, and a tag that blocks in one language and not the other quietly breaks it.

cases.comment: An authorized fill is a legitimate authoring decision. It is reported so a reviewer sees it — an authorized fill that leaves no trace is indistinguishable from an unauthorized one.
A bib entry without verified={true} did not come from doi2bib.py's DOI content negotiation — which is the one path the kit trusts.

cases.comment: NEGATIVE, and the case that found a live bug. Two stray backticks in ordinary prose — a unit, a quoted keystroke — used to pair up across the paragraphs between them and blank out every [@key] in that span. The citation then never entered `cited`, so a key with no bibliography entry was never reported missing and the blocking gate passed a manuscript it should have stopped. Nothing here looks like code; that is the point.

mutations.breaks: A key cited in the prose but absent from the bibliography stops being reported — the exact fabricated-citation shape the gate exists to stop.
[MATERIAL GAP] / [KANIT YOK] stops being detected, so a refused-to-fabricate hole passes the gate as if the section were finished.
Citation keys inside fenced code blocks are read as real citations, so any document that DOCUMENTS pandoc syntax reports invented missing keys.

Restores the newline-spanning `[^`]*` code-span pattern. Two stray backticks in ordinary prose then pair up across paragraphs and swallow every citation between them, so a cited key with no bibliography entry is silently never reported as missing — a false negative in the one check that blocks.
Machine-verified entries are reported as unverified and hand-written ones pass — the trust signal reversed.
drafts/STATUS.md is scanned as if it were manuscript prose, so the kit's own progress notes surface as citation defects.
replace: files = [f for f in files if f.exists() and f.name != "STATUS.md"]
